prompt.context: Cheapo Coffee roasts and packages coffee that it sells through coffee shops and grocery stores. Cheapo sells its product to these retailers and provides the labor to stock the shelves at store locations. The company has seen sales growth stagnate and profits decline over the last several years.
prompt.question: What is causing the decline and how can Cheapo Coffee raise its profits?

clarifying_info.a: Cheapo has two customers: the retailer and the end customer.

clarifying_info.q: Does Cheapo share data with retailers?
clarifying_info.a: Retailers share data on sales trends with Cheapo Coffee. A summary of one sales report can be seen in Exhibit 3.

clarifying_info.q: How has the overall industry performed?
clarifying_info.a: The overall industry has seen a similar stall in sales growth, but Cheapo has seen a larger decline in its profits relative to peers.

clarifying_info.q: Have there been any major corporate changes?
clarifying_info.a: Cheapo has not undergone any major corporate changes in the recent past.

clarifying_info.q: Has Cheapo taken any cost-cutting measures?
clarifying_info.a: Cheapo reduced overhead, but profitability continues to decline.

clarifying_info.q: What product lines does Cheapo sell?
clarifying_info.a: Cheapo sells branded, private label, and closeout products. Branded products are licensed from other companies and have the highest retail price. Private label products are produced with the retailers' logos and have the lowest retail price. Closeout products are branded products sold at a large discount (products that are about to expire or flavors going out of season).

clarifying_info.q: What is happening with the competitive landscape?
clarifying_info.a: The number of premium brands for coffee beans has increased in the past few years.

exhibits.title: Revenue Growth ($MM)
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing Cheapo Coffee's annual revenues from 2008 to 2012.
exhibits.data: Revenue bars for years 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012; scale runs from 0 to approximately 250 $MM; revenues appear to grow in early years then flatten.

exhibits.title: Profit Trends
exhibits.shows: A line chart showing Cheapo Coffee's profit margin (%) from 2008 to 2012.
exhibits.data: Profit margin scale from -1% to 8%; margin appears to start around 7% in 2008 and decline toward 0% or below by 2012.

exhibits.title: Revenue Breakdown
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing share of revenue by product type (Branded, Private Label, Closeout) for each year 2008 to 2012.
exhibits.data: Three product segments — Branded, Private Label, Closeout — shown as % of total revenue per year; Private Label share grows significantly over the period while Branded share shrinks.

exhibits.title: Cost as a Percentage of Sales
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing cost structure (Roasting/Packaging, Raw Materials, Gross Profit) as a percentage of sales for each of the three product lines: Branded, Private Label, and Closeout.
exhibits.data: Three product columns — Branded, Private Label, Closeout — each broken into Roasting/Packaging, Raw Materials, and Gross Profit as % of sales; scale 0% to 100%.

framework: Financials: Assess revenue trends (price vs. volume) and cost trends (COGS, variable costs, overhead)
Company: Evaluate changes in cost structure (variable vs. fixed split), sales and marketing focus, operational capabilities
Product: Examine product mix shift among Branded, Private Label, and Closeout lines; assess pricing dynamics and branding strength
Customer — End Customer: Investigate shifts in consumer preferences (e.g., negative caffeine studies), willingness to pay, channel preferences
Customer — Retailer: Assess retailer concentration and bargaining power impact on pricing
Industry/Competition: Evaluate new entrants, competitor pricing strategies, supplier concentration

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibits 1, 2, and 3, what hypothesis can you form about the cause of Cheapo's profit margin declines?
questions.guidance: Sales growth is slowing but not declining, so this is primarily a cost/margin issue rather than a revenue collapse. Exhibit 3 shows the product mix has shifted toward Private Label as a share of total revenue. Because Private Label carries the lowest retail price, the unit volume of Private Label has increased dramatically to sustain similar revenue levels. This volume increase drives up every variable cost (labor for shelf-stocking, transportation, roasting), causing profitability to decline.

questions.prompt: How would this product mix shift toward Private Label impact Cheapo's cost structure?
questions.guidance: An increase in the amount of volume handled causes an increase in every type of variable cost incurred by the company. The primary cost drivers are: (1) labor hours required to stock additional product — staff now stock a higher number of lower-priced Private Label packages to achieve the same sales level; (2) transportation costs increase with higher unit volume; (3) roasting costs increase proportionally with units processed.

questions.prompt: What information would you need to confirm this hypothesis?
questions.guidance: A cost breakdown for each product type is required to confirm whether the margin compression is driven by cost differences per unit across product lines.

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 4 and the provided retail prices (Branded $15/package, Closeouts $12, Private Label $4), does this confirm your hypothesis? What are Cheapo's profits on each product line?
questions.guidance: Exhibit 4 shows that Private Label profit margins as a percentage of sales are actually comparable to Branded product margins. However, the absolute dollar profit per unit tells a different story. The hypothesis is confirmed when absolute dollar profits are calculated: Private Label generates far less profit per package than Branded, so a volume shift toward Private Label dramatically reduces total profit even at similar margin percentages.

math.setup: Multiply retail price by gross profit margin % from Exhibit 4 to get profit per package. Branded margin ~20%, Closeout margin ~15%, Private Label margin ~20%.
steps: Private Label: $4 x 20% = $0.80 profit per package
math.answer: Cheapo earns $3.00 per Branded package, $1.80 per Closeout package, and only $0.80 per Private Label package. Even though margin percentages are similar, each Private Label bag generates far less absolute profit, so the volume shift to Private Label crushes total profits.

brainstorming.prompt: What actions can Cheapo Coffee take to address the profit decline caused by the shift toward Private Label?

categories.name: Reduce Private Label costs
ideas: Shelf Private Label products in a bargain bin instead of on shelves to reduce labor stocking time
Negotiate with retailers to have retailer staff stock Private Label rather than Cheapo staff
Optimize transportation routes and batch deliveries to reduce per-unit transport cost

categories.name: Shift product mix back toward higher-margin lines
ideas: Place Private Label product in a lower-traffic area of the store to reduce its visibility
Offer retailer incentives (co-op advertising, better margins) to promote Branded products
Invest in branding and marketing to increase consumer demand for Branded products

categories.name: Reprice Private Label
ideas: Raise prices on Private Label to reflect true cost structure
Introduce tiered Private Label pricing to capture more margin

recommendation: Cheapo Coffee's profit decline is driven by a product mix shift toward Private Label, which generates only $0.80 in profit per package versus $3.00 for Branded products. To raise profits, Cheapo should pursue two parallel tracks: (1) reduce the variable costs of handling Private Label volume (e.g., bargain bin display, shifting stocking responsibility to retailers), and (2) attempt to shift the sales mix back toward Branded and Closeout lines through retailer negotiations and targeted marketing.
risks: Retailer incentives may not align with Cheapo's interests — retailers may use Private Label coffee as a value marketing tool to drive traffic and resist any push to reduce Private Label volume or raise prices
Raising Private Label prices could cause retailers to switch to competitor suppliers
Consumers may have already shifted preferences toward lower-priced options, limiting the ability to reignite Branded demand
next_steps: Benchmark per-unit costs for Private Label products produced by competitors to identify cost reduction opportunities
Approach retailers to negotiate either a price increase on Private Label or alternative shelf arrangements (bargain bin, retailer self-stocking) that reduce Cheapo's labor costs
Analyze which retail partners have the most favorable economics and prioritize renegotiations with them first
